suggestions.quote: the hospital is one set kit (counter, bench, ward) re-lit
suggestions.fix: The kit-reuse call is sound. Add a reuse list to the outline. Reused: ward, bench, counter, bus, office, hourglass device. New: phone-app prop, patient wristband, pillow bill, photo, aged-head variants for you, Papa and the invigilator. Build the aged heads as eyebrow, hair and wrinkle overlays on the existing rig, not new rigs, so they are not the long pole.

suggestions.quote: you sit the exam older than the invigilator
suggestions.fix: This implies an exam hall and a pharmacy, both new sets. Stage each as a one-layer insert (a desk row and a pharmacy counter re-lit from the hospital counter), not a full set. Say so in the outline.

suggestions.quote: the hours peel off your figure as Papa watches
suggestions.fix: Show the hours as a split-flap counter or a stamped tag, not free-floating text, because style.md allows only those. Peel off one flap per 2 to 3 s so something changes.

suggestions.quote: each work-hour card folds into a year and drops off your figure
suggestions.fix: Same rule: no loose text cards. Fold stamped tags into year-tags. For the wordless peak, name the 2 to 4 s changes inside the 10 s: card folds, hair greys, camera drifts to the bench, the hands and the wristband. Keep one slow-motion ghost, and keep Papa and you in colour while the world is grey.

suggestions.quote: his patient wristband lies between your identical-looking hands
suggestions.fix: Draw the wristband blank, with no printed name or text. Stage it as a top-down insert, then a side-on two-shot on the bench. A face reaction (relieved or afraid) follows within 2 s of the wristband reveal.

suggestions.quote: Papa, after his surgery, teases you about your bus pass
suggestions.fix: Add `> BUBBLE: Papa: Bus pass again, beta?` (four words). Say the trigger gesture, Papa tapping your pass, now so line 39 can mirror it.

suggestions.quote: He's teasing you about the bus pass again. You let him.
suggestions.fix: Keep the bus-pass tap as the same gesture and prop. Keep the end-card tags in the left two-thirds and the right third quiet from the last 15 s.

suggestions.quote: The turn breaks your own line
suggestions.fix: The G2 `cues.yaml` is not in my inputs, so I could not check it. Ask for one with a one-word intent per beat, for example hush (opening), light (first jump), dread (decade), hollow (peak), warm (return). Change the cue at or after the wristband reveal, not before it, so music follows the story.

suggestions.quote: the phone lit with an hourglass and one red button
suggestions.fix: Give the rule device its own sound hook: a sand tick on each tap, thinner each time. Note it for the cue sheet. The hourglass is both the tap-counter prop and the greying device, so keep one hourglass design everywhere.
